Node2vec's parameters set the walk's search strategy. Low return parameter p and low in-out parameter q (DFS-like walks) move outward through the graph and capture homophily, meaning nodes in the same densely connected community get similar embeddings. High q (BFS-like walks) stays in the local neighborhood and captures structural equivalence, meaning nodes with similar roles or neighborhood structure get similar embeddings even if they are far apart. A cluster that reflects homophily should therefore be a community, not a set of structurally equivalent nodes. If the blue cluster is described as structural equivalence, that would more plausibly come from BFS-style sampling, or the cluster may be a community that happens to share structural roles. Please share the figure or the paper's exact parameter settings if you need a definitive account of that specific network.
